public_body: Gloucester City Council Planning And Development Committee
overall: The AG found no evidence of a secret drafting meeting, but found that an email exchange between a quorum of the three-member committee about the zoning amendment was an illegal deliberation; declined the non-OML allegation.

allegations.summary: Alleged that committee members met or communicated privately outside an open meeting to rewrite a proposed zoning amendment.
allegations.key_passage: We have found no evidence in our review of the Committee's communications to suggest that the Committee members met or communicated outside of an open meeting to draft the Birdseye Mixed-Use Overlay District zoning amendment, as alleged by the complainant.

allegations.summary: A quorum of the three-member committee discussed the draft zoning amendment by email, outside a posted open meeting.
allegations.key_passage: With this email exchange, the Committee engaged in a written communication between a quorum of the members regarding "public business within its jurisdiction."

allegations.summary: Alleged that committee or city staff aligned with a developer before adequate public review of a zoning amendment; not an Open Meeting Law claim.
allegations.key_passage: Because this portion of the complaint does not allege a violation of the Open Meeting Law, G.L. c. 30A, §§ 18-25, we decline to address it.

remedy: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law
the Committee publicly disclose at its next meeting copies of the November 15, 2010 emails that resulted in this violation
remedy_passage: We order immediate and future compliance with the Open Meeting Law, and caution the Committee that a determination by our office of shnilar violations in the future may be considered evidence of intent to violate the Open Meeting Law. Additionally, we order the Committee to publicly disclose at its next meeting copies of the November 15, 2010 emails
